$comment: Every place in the corpus where Cord fell back to carrying a raw App Definition fragment instead
CordCoverageTests asserts this list matches the raw pointers EXACTLY -- not as a subset. That is
deliberate and it cuts both ways: adding an escape hatch requires a reviewed line here, and
removing modelling that used to exist fails the build instead of quietly lowering a percentage.
An entry is (app, pointer, reason). `app` is the definition's `key`; `pointer` is a JSON Pointer
into the App Definition. `reason` is for the human reading the diff: say what is unmodelled and
why that is acceptable for now, not that a test demanded an entry.
SCOPE: entities and behaviour (processes, commands, workflows, roles). Sections still owned by a
later slice -- pages, views, theme, presentation, archetype, relations, plugins, and the

entries.reason: `emits` publishes a domain event other automation can subscribe to. It is real vocabulary and it is deliberately NOT on a transition: eventing is a behaviour-to-behaviour wire, and modelling it here would mean designing the subscriber side too. Two occurrences, both in one app.

clone_scenario -- the command this transition names carries `emits`, which has no home on a transition, so the fold was REFUSED and both halves stay as the document filed them. This is the importer's unfold path working: rather than drop `emits`, it leaves the transition naming its command and lets that command survive as a standalone action. Costs two pointers and keeps the round trip exact.
shift_hire_start -- same unfold as above: its command carries `emits`.
The idempotency key of the same createForEach is an ARRAY of field keys (a composite), not a single one. Declined for the same reason and carried whole.

createForEach `source` is an OBJECT here -- {range:{from,count,step}} -- generating a row per month rather than iterating an existing collection. CordEffect types Source as a string, so the importer correctly declines it rather than modelling it half-right. One occurrence; a generator source is its own construct and wants its own shape, not a widened string.

The idempotency key of the same createForEach is an ARRAY of field keys (a composite), not a single one. Declined for the same reason and carried raw. Generates one lifecycle row per adoption point, per segment.

createForEach `source` is an OBJECT here -- {entity, filters} -- iterating an existing collection rather than a generated range. Cord's aggregate vocabulary models a filtered read over an entity, but not yet as the SOURCE of a generative effect, so the object is carried raw. Generates one lifecycle row per adoption point, per segment.

The idempotency key of the same createForEach is an ARRAY of field keys (a composite), not a single one. Declined for the same reason and carried raw. Generates one cohort row per lifecycle step, per acquisition. This one builds the cohort grid the Cordango revenue model needs: month m's revenue is every live cohort at its own age, which a rollup cannot express because it aggregates one field rather than multiplying two rows.

intake_form.route_to_person -- `mapsTo` is a FIELD ROLE that wires a form question to the field it fills on the record the submission creates. It is half of a two-sided declaration (the other half is role:targetEntity on the form entity), so modelling it as a lone string property would represent the mechanism rather than the intent. It belongs with the Forms intake surface in the UI slice.

Per-field permission inside a grant -- read/write narrowed for individual fields. A genuine construct and the only field-level security in the corpus; modelling it means deciding how field rules compose with entity rules, which is a security question and not a lowering one. Two occurrences.

The starting state is CONDITIONAL here -- {rules:[{when,state}],fallback} -- so a standard-tier room is auto-approved while everything else starts pending. CordProcess types InitialState as a state key, so this is carried whole. One occurrence, and widening the type to 'string or rules object' would put a union in the ops schema for a single app.

task.effort -- a display-only subtree rollup on a self-nesting entity, rendered as `own (subtree total)`. It is an aggregate, so it wants to be a CordCalc variant rather than a boolean-ish flag, but it aggregates over the entity's own parent chain rather than through a reference and does not fit CordAggregate as it stands. Modelling it as a third calc kind is small and deliberate work, not a passthrough.
